subtitle: Exile, Ink and the Return of a Mountain King

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a solitary king on a jungle ridge, distant sea and ships beyond
panels.action: Govinda Manikya stands weary yet unbowed on a misty hilltop, jungle slopes of Tripura behind him and the shimmering Bay of Bengal with small Arakanese ships ahead, his hand resting on a rolled manuscript at his waist.

dialogue.text: Driven out by a brother and Mughal guns, Govinda Manikya walks through jungle and sea to Arakan—then returns to Tripura with borrowed power, and leaves behind not just a throne, but a book.

i18n.hi: भाई और मुग़ल तोपों से निकाला गया गोविंदा माणिक्य जंगल और समंदर पार कर अराकान पहुँचा—फिर उधारी ताक़त लेकर त्रिपुरा लौटा, और पीछे सिर्फ़ सिंहासन नहीं, एक किताब भी छोड़ गया।

panels.shot: dim interior medium shot, throne room, low angle on king overshadowed by looming Mughal envoy silhouettes
panels.action: Govinda Manikya sits on a carved Tripuri throne in a darkened hall, his face lit by oil lamps as distant Mughal envoys in turbans stand in the shadows with scrolls and demands.

dialogue.text: In the mid-seventeenth century, Tripura’s hills stood between Bengal and the eastern sea, watching the Mughal Empire press closer with every season.

i18n.hi: सत्रहवीं सदी के बीचोंबीच, त्रिपुरा की पहाड़ियाँ बंगाल और पूरबी समंदर के बीच खड़ी थीं, हर मौसम के साथ आगे बढ़ते मुग़ल साम्राज्य को देखते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of palace courtyard, tension-filled, brother’s soldiers entering from gate while loyalists look uncertain
panels.action: Govinda Manikya turns sharply in a palace courtyard as armored Tripuri soldiers, now bearing standards of his brother Chhatra Manikya, stride in under a monsoon sky while courtiers shrink back.

dialogue.text: When Mughal-backed Chhatra Manikya moved against him, Govinda’s court splintered in a day. Some saw safety in the new tide; others saw only the dust of retreat.

i18n.hi: जब मुग़लों के सहारे छत्र माणिक्य ने उस पर चढ़ाई की, तो एक ही दिन में गोविंदा का दरबार बिखर गया। कुछ ने नई लहर में पनाह देखी, कुछ ने बस पीछे हटती धूल।

panels.shot: tight medium on Govinda in simple travel garb, torchlit corridor, sense of haste
panels.action: Govinda Manikya, stripped of royal ornaments and dressed in plain cloth and a light cloak, strides down a narrow stone corridor lit by a single torch, jaw clenched, a small bundle and sword in hand.

dialogue.speaker: govinda_manikya
dialogue.text: A throne can be taken in a night. A kingdom’s memory cannot.

i18n.hi: सिंहासन रातों-रात छिन सकता है। यादों का राज नहीं।

panels.shot: high wide shot over dense forest and steep ridges, tiny caravan threading through
panels.action: A tiny line of riders and porters, with Govinda Manikya at their head, winds cautiously along a narrow path clinging to a steep, forested slope in the Chittagong Hill Tracts under heavy clouds.

dialogue.text: He slipped away through the Chittagong Hill Tracts, those steep green ribs between Tripura and the coast, where paths vanish in mist and ambush sits behind each rock.

i18n.hi: वह चिटगाँग पहाड़ी इलाकों से फिसल कर निकला, वे तीखी हरी पसलियाँ जो त्रिपुरा को तट से जोड़ती हैं, जहाँ राहें धुंध में खो जाती हैं और हर चट्टान के पीछे घात बैठा है।

panels.shot: low, intimate campfire shot, close on Govinda writing by firelight while others sleep
panels.action: Beside a small campfire under towering trees, Govinda Manikya sits awake while his few followers sleep; he traces lines on a palm leaf with a stylus, face lit by the trembling flame.

dialogue.text: Exile stripped him of court drums and banners. It did not strip him of ink; even in flight, he kept notes, names, lines of old tales, as if holding the kingdom on a page.

i18n.hi: निर्वासन ने उसके नगाड़े और झंडे छीन लिए। स्याही नहीं छिनी; भागते हुए भी वह नोट लिखता रहा—नाम, क़िस्से, पुरानी कहानियों की पंक्तियाँ, जैसे पूरे राज को एक पन्ने पर थामे हो।

panels.shot: wide coastal shot, boats rocking at dawn, jungle meeting sea
panels.action: At first light, Govinda Manikya stands on a muddy creek bank where the forest thins to mangroves, watching small wooden boats rock gently, Arakanese sailors preparing to push off toward the open sea.

dialogue.text: Beyond those hills lay the Bay of Bengal. Beyond the waves lay Arakan—a coastal kingdom that traded in rice, horses, salt, and in the exiles of other courts.

i18n.hi: उन पहाड़ियों के आगे बंगाल की खाड़ी थी। लहरों के पार अराकान—एक तटीय राज जहाँ चावल, घोड़े, नमक और दूसरे दरबारों के निर्वासितों की सौदेबाज़ी होती थी।

panels.shot: medium shot on boat deck, sea horizon, Govinda gripping rail as spray hits
panels.action: On the deck of a small boat heaving over low waves, Govinda Manikya grips the wooden rail, spray catching his face as the coastline of Bengal fades into a hazy line behind him.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala later claimed he met the exiled Mughal prince Shah Shuja on this Arakan shore—but when historians weigh the dates, that meeting dissolves. The legends reach, the chronology refuses.

i18n.hi: राजमाला कहती है कि यहाँ उसने मुग़ल शहज़ादा, निर्वासित शाह शुजा से मुलाक़ात की—पर जब इतिहासकार तारीख़ें तौलते हैं, वह मुलाक़ात धुंध बन कर उड़ जाती है। क़िस्से बढ़ते हैं, समय-रेखा नहीं मानती।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mrauk U-like cityscape, pagodas and forts, bustling harbor
panels.action: Govinda Manikya stands at the edge of a bustling Arakanese harbor, watching rows of wooden houses and rising temple spires of Mrauk U beyond, as soldiers in distinctive helmets patrol the quay.

dialogue.text: He came instead into the orbit of Sanda Thudhamma, king of Arakan, whose court looked west to Bengal, east to the hills, and saw opportunity in Tripura’s quarrels.

i18n.hi: असल में वह सांदा थुधम्मा के घेरे में आया, अराकान के उस राजा के, जिसकी निगाह पश्चिम में बंगाल पर, पूरब में पहाड़ों पर थी, और जिसे त्रिपुरा के झगड़ों में मौक़ा दिखा।

panels.shot: interior audience hall wide, Sanda Thudhamma implied as unseen figure on dais, Govinda bowing
panels.action: Inside a long wooden audience hall adorned with carved beams, Govinda Manikya bows deeply before an unseen figure on a raised platform, Arakanese courtiers seated cross-legged along the sides watching with measured interest.

dialogue.text: Arakan’s chronicles remember a network of alliances and raids stretching into Chittagong. In this web, a dispossessed Tripuri raja was both burden and bargaining chip.

i18n.hi: अराकान की तवारीख़ चिटगाँग तक फैले गठबंधनों और धावे का जाल याद रखती हैं। इसी जाल में एक बे–घर त्रिपुरी राजा बोझ भी था, सौदे की गोटी भी।

panels.shot: medium shot profile of Govinda and an Arakanese minister, map between them
panels.action: Govinda Manikya leans over a parchment map with an Arakanese minister in a simple yet rich robe; their fingers trace the line of the Feni and Gomati rivers towards Tripura’s hills.

dialogue.speaker: govinda_manikya
dialogue.text: You gain a friend at Bengal’s shoulder. I gain a road back home.

i18n.hi: तुम्हें बंगाल की कोहनी पर एक दोस्त। मुझे घर लौटने की राह।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of mixed Arakanese and Tripuri forces marching along river plain
panels.action: A column of Arakanese soldiers with spears and conical helmets marches beside Tripuri warriors along a river plain, Govinda Manikya riding at the front on a small horse, eyes fixed on the distant blue rise of his homeland hills.

dialogue.text: Around 1667, the tide turned. With Arakanese support and Tripura’s own factions shifting again, Govinda rode back, not as a wandering exile now, but as a claimant with foreign steel at his side.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1667 में फ़िज़ा बदल गई। अराकानी मदद और त्रिपुरा के बदलते गुटों के सहारे, गोविंदा लौट पड़ा—अब भटका निर्वासित नहीं, विदेशी फ़ौलाद के साथ दावा करने वाला राजा।

panels.shot: wide shot of hill-fort silhouette at dusk, armies facing off at a distance
panels.action: At dusk, a Tripuri hill-fort crowns a ridge while two bodies of troops face each other in the valley below—Arakanese banners fluttering on one side, Tripuri standards on both, torches already flickering as tension hangs in the air.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala speaks of struggles and counter-struggles, of brothers set against brothers, of forts taken and retaken. It names Govinda’s restoration, but leaves the smoke and cries between the lines.

i18n.hi: राजमाला लड़ाइयों–मुक़ाबलों की बात करती है—भाइयों के आमने–सामने आने की, क़िलों के छिनने और फिर छिन जाने की। वह गोविंदा की वापसी का नाम तो लेती है, पर धुएँ और चीखें लाइनों के बीच छोड़ देती है।

panels.shot: medium low-angle of Govinda on palace steps, people bowing or watching cautiously
panels.action: Govinda Manikya ascends the worn stone steps of the Tripuri palace, flanked by a small Arakanese guard, as townspeople watch from a distance, some bowing deeply, others peering with guarded eyes.

dialogue.text: In time, Chhatra’s moment passed. Govinda Manikya was restored to the Manikya throne, his return owed not only to his own resolve, but to Arakanese arms and the ever-shifting currents of Mughal frontier politics.

i18n.hi: आख़िरकार, छत्र का दौर ढल गया। गोविंदा माणिक्य फिर माणिक्य-सिंहासन पर बैठा—उसकी वापसी सिर्फ़ उसकी जिद से नहीं, अराकानी तलवारों और मुग़ल सरहद की बदलती सियासत से भी लिखी गई।

panels.shot: interior throne room medium, Govinda seated, Arakanese officers respectfully taking leave
panels.action: In the reopened Tripuri throne hall, Govinda Manikya sits robed as king while a small group of Arakanese officers in their own attire bow slightly before turning to depart, Tripuri nobles looking on in complicated silence.

dialogue.speaker: govinda_manikya
dialogue.text: Foreign hands opened this door. What we build inside must be our own.

i18n.hi: यह दरवाज़ा पराए हाथों ने खोला है। अंदर जो बनायेंगे, वह हमारा होगा।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot, Govinda with scholars around a low table of manuscripts
panels.action: Govinda Manikya sits cross-legged with three Brahmin scribes and poets around a low wooden table piled with palm-leaf bundles, his finger resting on a leaf as he speaks and they listen intently.

dialogue.text: His years back on the throne left more than edicts. Under his patronage, the third canto of the Rajmala took shape, weaving his own rise, fall, and return into the long song of Tripura’s kings.

i18n.hi: उसके दोबारा राज में लौटने से सिर्फ़ फ़रमान नहीं बचे। उसकी सरपरस्ती में राजमाला का तीसरा कांड बना, जिसमें उसका उठना, गिरना और लौटना, त्रिपुरा के राजाओं के लंबे गीत में बुना गया।

panels.shot: close-up on hands writing Bengali script on palm leaf, faint outline of Vishnu image behind
panels.action: A close view shows Govinda Manikya’s steady hand guiding a stylus as Bengali script forms on a palm leaf, a small painted image of Vishnu set on a low altar in the blurred background.

dialogue.text: Tradition links his court to a Bengali rendering of the Brihannaradiya Purana, bringing old Sanskrit verses of devotion and duty closer to the tongue of his eastern subjects.

i18n.hi: रिवाज़ उसके दरबार को बृहन्नारदिय पुराण के एक बांग्ला रूपांतर से जोड़ता है, जिससे भक्ति और धर्म के पुराने संस्कृत श्लोक उसके पूरबी प्रजाजनों की ज़बान के क़रीब आए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Govinda by window, Rajmala manuscript in hand, view of hills outside
panels.action: Govinda Manikya stands by a carved window, holding a bound stack of palm leaves—the Rajmala’s fresh canto—looking out over the layered green hills of Tripura in the soft light of late afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: govinda_manikya
dialogue.text: One day, they will forget the marches and the bargains. Let them not forget the path.

i18n.hi: एक दिन, लोग मार्च और सौदे भूल जायेंगे। राह को न भूलें।

panels.shot: montage-style wide: ghosted overlay of Tagore writing in a much later study, with Tripura hills faint behind Govinda
panels.action: Govinda Manikya’s calm profile fills one side of the frame against a faint backdrop of Tripura’s hills, while on the other, in a translucent overlay of a later century, Rabindranath Tagore sits at a desk in a Calcutta study, pen poised over paper.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Tagore would take Tripura’s remembered king and turn him into the Rajarshi of fiction, but the man himself remains in the chronicles—a ruler who returned with foreign aid, and chose to strengthen memory as much as power.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, टैगोर ने इसी याद किए गए त्रिपुरी राजा को अपनी कहानी का ‘राजर्षि’ बना दिया, पर असली आदमी आज भी इतिहास में दर्ज है—एक शासक जो पराई मदद से लौटा, और जिसने ताक़त जितनी, याद को भी मज़बूत करना चुना।

title_i18n.hi: गोविंदा माणिक्य अराकान से लौटता है

subtitle_i18n.en: Exile, Ink and the Return of a Mountain King
subtitle_i18n.hi: निर्वासन, स्याही और एक पर्वत-राजा की वापसी
